journal: The Lancet Oncology
title: [Comment] Time to act: a global call for oral cancer prevention and early detection
abstract: Oral cancer, ranked among the 16th most common cancers globally, represents a major public health burden.1 In some countries in south Asia, oral cancer is the most frequent cancer among men. A recent systematic analysis for the Global Burden of Disease study concluded that insufficient action in the past three decades has led to little change in population oral health, underscoring the necessity for renewed strategic focus.2
authors: Delphine Maret, Saman Warnakulasuriya, Joel B Epstein, Thomas Geeraerts, Emmanuelle Vigarios

journal: The Lancet Oncology
title: [Articles] Evaluation of progression-free status at 24 months as a surrogate endpoint for overall survival in patients with human papillomavirus-positive oropharyngeal cancer: a retrospective cohort study
abstract: Progression-free status at 24 months was a strong prognostic marker for overall survival at the patient level in HPV-positive oropharyngeal cancer and future trial-level analysis is now warranted. The adoption of this endpoint has the potential to accelerate therapeutic development by enabling earlier evaluation of treatment activity, thereby facilitating the timely introduction of novel therapies to this patient population before the availability of mature overall survival data.
authors: Caineng Cao, Eric J Sherman, Nadeem Riaz, Sean M McBride, Yao Yu, Achraf Shamseddine, Winston Wong, Lara A Dunn, Alan L Ho, Richard J Wong, Nancy Y Lee

journal: JAMA Current Issue
title: Head and Neck Cancer: A Review
abstract: This review examines the epidemiology, risk factors, clinical presentation, diagnosis, and treatment of head and neck squamous cell carcinomas of the upper aerodigestive tract.

journal: JAMA Otolaryngology–Head & Neck Surgery Current Issue
title: JAMA Otolaryngology–Head & Neck Surgery
abstract: Mission Statement: To advance the patient-centered, evidence-based practice of otolaryngology–head and neck surgery by publishing scientifically rigorous and innovative research, reviews, and commentary. Our journal serves as a vital resource for clinicians, researchers, educators, and trainees by providing high-quality, peer-reviewed content focused on improving the understanding and treatment of ear, nose, and throat conditions. We are dedicated to fostering dialogue and action on critical issues in otolaryngology, including the education and training of health care professionals, quality improvement, and the ethics and economics of equitable health care delivery.

journal: JAMA Otolaryngology–Head & Neck Surgery Current Issue
title: Patient-Reported Outcomes Across Treatment Strategies in Papillary Thyroid Microcarcinoma
abstract: This systematic review and meta-analysis explores active surveillance vs surgery or thermal ablation on patient-reported health-related quality of life outcomes in studies in patients with papillary thyroid microcarcinoma.

journal: JAMA Otolaryngology–Head & Neck Surgery Current Issue
title: Pathologic Response and Survival After Neoadjuvant Immunotherapy for HNSCC
abstract: This systematic review and meta-analysis assesses the association between achievement of a pathologic treatment response and improvement in disease-free survival in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC).

journal: JAMA Otolaryngology–Head & Neck Surgery Current Issue
title: Thyroid Lobectomy and Neck Dissection for N1b Papillary Thyroid Carcinoma
abstract: This cohort study examines recurrence and survival outcomes in propensity-matched thyroid lobectomy vs total thyroidectomy + radioactive iodine patients who presented with ipsilateral N1b papillary thyroid carcinoma.

journal: JAMA Otolaryngology–Head & Neck Surgery Current Issue
title: Pembrolizumab in Head and Neck Cancer—Promise and Price
abstract: This Viewpoint considers the financial impact of expanding the indication of pembrolizumab for treatment of resectable locally advanced head and neck squamous cell carcinoma expressing programmed cell death 1 ligand 1.

journal: JAMA Otolaryngology–Head & Neck Surgery Current Issue
title: Hoarseness With Supraglottic Ulcer in an Immunocompetent Adult
abstract: A 61-year-old man presented to the otolaryngology clinic with a 2-month history of progressive hoarseness, dysphagia, odynophagia, and persistent globus sensation. What is your diagnosis?

journal: JAMA Otolaryngology–Head & Neck Surgery Current Issue
title: Biofeedback vs Respiratory Retraining for Inducible Laryngeal Obstruction
abstract: This randomized clinical trial evaluates the effectiveness of video biofeedback compared with respiratory retraining therapy in the treatment of episodic, inhalational dyspnea attributed to inducible laryngeal obstruction.

journal: JAMA Otolaryngology–Head & Neck Surgery Current Issue
title: Factors Associated With Opioid Refills After Otolaryngology–Head and Neck Surgery
abstract: This cohort study examines perioperative risk factors associated with opioid refill prescriptions within 90 days after discharge among adults patients who underwent otolaryngology–head and neck surgery procedures.

journal: JAMA Otolaryngology–Head & Neck Surgery Current Issue
title: Osteoradionecrosis After Radiotherapy for Oropharyngeal Carcinoma
abstract: This cohort study characterizes the incidence, severity, and predictors of osteoradionecrosis in patients with oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma treated with curative-intent radiotherapy and compares outcomes between those receiving proton therapy vs intensity-modulated radiation therapy.

journal: JAMA Otolaryngology–Head & Neck Surgery Current Issue
title: Treatment Interruption and Outcomes in Head and Neck Cancer
abstract: This secondary analysis of 3 randomized clinical trials examines the association of radiotherapy interruptions with locoregional failure and overall survival for patients with head and neck squamous cell carcinoma.

journal: JAMA Otolaryngology–Head & Neck Surgery Current Issue
title: Serum Metabolomics for Prognostic Stratification in Resected Advanced-Stage Oral Cavity Cancer
abstract: This cohort study identifies serum metabolites associated with oral cavity squamous cell carcinoma recurrence and develops and validates a prognostic scoring system.

journal: JAMA Otolaryngology–Head & Neck Surgery Current Issue
title: Vertebral Lesions in a Patient With Salivary Duct Carcinoma
abstract: A 62-year-old man with a history of submandibular salivary duct, alcohol use disorder, and facial flushing after small amounts of alcohol presented with diminished superficial sensation, dysesthesia, and impaired proprioception in the lower extremities. What is your diagnosis?

journal: JAMA Otolaryngology–Head & Neck Surgery Current Issue
title: Reframing Head and Neck Cancer Costs—Insights from Screening in Taiwan
abstract: To the Editor Villemure-Poliquin et al identify stage and multimodality treatment as the strongest factors associated with high first-year costs in head and neck cancer. We commend the population-based approach, but 3 issues merit clarification and qualification.

journal: JAMA Otolaryngology–Head & Neck Surgery Current Issue
title: Reframing Head and Neck Cancer Costs—Insights from Screening in Taiwan—Reply
abstract: In Reply We thank Wu et al for their interest in our article. We have responded to the 3 questions that they raised.

journal: JAMA Otolaryngology–Head & Neck Surgery Online First
title: Proposed Version Nine of the AJCC and UICC TNM Classification for Salivary Gland Carcinoma
abstract: This prognostic study derives and validates a salivary gland carcinoma–specific pathological tumor-node-metastasis (TNM) classification with improved prognostic accuracy and optimized stage distribution for version nine of the American Joint Committee on Cancer (AJCC)/Union for International Cancer Control (UICC) TNM staging protocol.

journal: JAMA Otolaryngology–Head & Neck Surgery Online First
title: Radiomics in Otolaryngology–Head and Neck Surgery
abstract: This Review describes radiomics and how they can enhance diagnosis, optimize prognostication, and personalize treatment in otolaryngology.

journal: JAMA Otolaryngology–Head & Neck Surgery Online First
title: Thyroidectomy Outcomes in Older Adults
abstract: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluates the association of older age (≥65 years) with thyroidectomy safety by comparing endocrine-related complications and mortality between older and younger patients.

journal: JAMA Otolaryngology–Head & Neck Surgery Online First
title: Large Language Models and Otolaryngology
abstract: This Narrative Review examines the evolving landscape of the application of large language models, highlighting innovations from other medical specialties, to provide otolaryngologists with the knowledge and direction needed to advance the field.
